title: Irreducible phenomenal information leads to epiphenomenalism

statements.text: Lewis argued that anyone who holds there is phenomenal information irreducibly different from physical information is led to a form of epiphenomenalism, whatever they say about identity or causation. Two possible phenomenal contents of the taste of Vegemite fit all the same physical information, so which one is actual makes no physical difference. Lewis used this against phenomenal information, but it ties the knowledge argument to epiphenomenalism.

sources.quote: one will still be led to a form of epiphenomenalism if one says there is phenomenal information that is irreducibly different from physical information
